complexity.notes: The try/except around the comparison loops is unidiomatic and masks potential bugs; a plain length check plus one comparison loop (or simply multiset_s == multiset_t) would be cleaner. The redundant second loop is unnecessary since equal-sized multisets with matching counts for s's keys already match t's. Consider collections.Counter for the multiset logic.
complexity.summary: Builds character-frequency multisets for both strings via dicts, then compares the two multisets key-by-key (in both directions) to verify equality. Because keys are lowercase English letters, each dict holds at most 26 entries, so all lookups are O(1) even in the worst case.
